_comment: Note 655's shape with synthetic names: two children in one exchange, a different observation about each. EXPECTED TO FAIL — see evals/README.md, 'Known-red fixtures'. The transcript joins the two children in ONE clause, which note 655's own wording does not: measured on the canonical model, the comma-separated original ('...with Bruno, and Bruno had to be...') splits correctly 2 of 4 runs. A 2/4 row is a coin flip in the baseline, useless as a regression signal, so this fixture removes the clause boundary and pins the limitation where it is structural instead: a clause is the smallest unit a span can hold and a span carries one summary, so one clause about two children can only produce one piece of text. Whichever way the model labels it, a child gets the other's observation or nothing. The 2/4 matters on its own — the merge the plan accepted as a limitation is intermittent, not constant, so a per-span summarisation call would buy less than the plan assumed. Nadia and Bruno are far apart phonetically on purpose: the only thing this fixture can fail on is the merge, never name resolution. Delete the red row here when a per-span summarisation call lands, not before.
